correctness.rationale: For N=2n≥4, compatible cyclic adjacency pairs form a cycle matching. Counting marked selected edges and positive gaps gives N/(N−k) times binom(N−k,k); multiplying by k! and the probability of the required pairs yields the factorial-moment product. Its recurrence has factor 1+(1−k)/(N−k−1), and all moments are bounded by N/(N−1), including the extension by zero above n. Set b_k=k(3−k)/2. For k≤N/4 the recurrence first gives a_{N,k}−1=O((k+1)²/N). Subtracting (b_{k+1}−b_k)/N gives incremental error O((k+1)³/N²), so telescoping gives O((k+1)^4/N²). For k>N/4 the moment bound and |b_k|=O((k+1)²) are absorbed by that same estimate, even above n. Factorial summability on |z|≤2 now bounds the PGF remainder uniformly, and Cauchy's coefficient bound controls each r≥0, including r>n. Extracting (-z²+4z−3)e^(z−1)/(4n) gives the local correction. Its Poisson-weighted signed mass is zero and the positive coefficients are 1,3,3,1 before factorial weighting at r=1,2,3,4; their factorial-weighted sum is 73/24. The l¹ remainder is O(n^(-2)), giving 73/(96en) against the fixed Poisson target, with the claimed negative r=0 correction.
residual_risks: Enumeration corroborates the finite counting identity, not the uniform analytic estimate. The result is for n≥2 and the full cyclic set of allowed pairs, not the path or mean-matched variant.
